title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
why_read: A theoretical math paper on neural network expressivity using topology, interesting mainly to researchers in deep learning theory rather than practitioners.
analysis: This paper studies how complex a neural network's output shape can be, measured using topological invariants called Betti numbers, which count holes and connected components in high-dimensional space. The authors give explicit network architectures (specific layer sizes) that provably can produce outputs with arbitrarily complex topology, improving on prior bounds via a clever construction using products of spheres. This is a pure theory contribution with no empirical results, useful for people studying fundamental limits of neural network expressiveness rather than applied engineers.
